A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continual-learning framework, renamed from MoRA to MoRAM. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIP and language-model experiments, code-generation and generalization results, routing ablations and activation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds TRACE and SuperNI evaluations, post-pruning experiments and aggregated activation analysis.

M1.justification: The core rank-1 experts, self-activation, top-k masking, temperature scaling and inference thresholding remain unchanged. v3 additionally specifies and evaluates optional storage pruning after each task, retaining atoms covering 99% of cumulative training activation (Section 3.3.4 and Appendix A.10), beyond v2's per-input activation pruning.

E1.justification: v3 adds TRACE's heterogeneous continual-learning stream, including MeetingBank summarization, Py150 code generation and 20Minuten multilingual simplification, and adds SuperNI evaluation. This substantially broadens language-task coverage beyond the retained classification streams and single-stage CodeAlpaca fine-tuning experiments.

E2.justification: New evaluated comparators include FIX(ICL), OGD, GEM, DualPrompt, HiDeLoRA and TreeLoRA in TRACE Table 2, and SAPT and C-LoRA in SuperNI Table 13. Earlier comparison sets remain; the renamed routing-ablation variants correspond to their v2 counterparts.

E3.justification: TRACE introduces three backbone configurations, 5,000 training and 2,000 testing examples per task, a variable epoch schedule, task-specific metrics and OP/BWT evaluation. SuperNI adds protocols with and without generated replay. These are settings for added experiments; the stated settings of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of the storage–accuracy trade-off from post-pruning (Table 19), order sensitivity using existing task-order results (Table 14), and whether illustrative rank-reuse patterns hold across entire task test sets (Figure 5). Earlier routing, sparsity, temperature and activation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 14 newly reports standard deviations across the three existing task orders, including 77.6 ± 0.26 for MoRAM. This measures order variability rather than additional random-seed runs. The earlier three-run X-TAIL uncertainty reporting remains unchanged; TRACE follows the same mean-and-standard-deviation practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial TRACE, SuperNI, pruning and activation results. For example, TRACE reports LLaMA-2-7B-Chat OP 44.54 ± 0.9 and BWT 1.37 ± 0.3; Table 19 reports Last accuracy of 79.5 with pruning versus 80.9 without it. Retained benchmark values match v2. A small inconsistency appears in new Table 14: L2P's mean is 61.0, while retained Table 8 still gives 60.7.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and the reorganized method equations restate the existing associative-memory factorization and sparse rank mixture. Redundant algebra is condensed, and standard OP/BWT formulas explain the added evaluation metrics. No substantive new theoretical result, proof or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Despite renaming and stronger emphasis on associative memory, both versions claim that sparse, self-routed rank-1 experts improve knowledge reuse, reduce interference and forgetting, and preserve generalization efficiently. The memory interpretation already appears in v2; the new experiments support these retained core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of replay compatibility, order robustness and aggregated routing patterns, and explicitly discusses linear storage growth and pruning trade-offs. It distinguishes static weight-memory keys from dynamic attention keys and adds application, bias and misuse discussion. The central specialization and forgetting explanations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a TRACE implementation recipe covering hyperparameters, context length, epoch schedule, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, BF16 and four H100 GPUs, plus the post-pruning procedure. Existing experiment recipes remain. v2's promise to release source code upon acceptance is removed without replacement access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted positioning against TreeLoRA, HiDe-PET and SAPT, references TRACE and SuperNI, and adds fine-grained MoE literature. It removes model-editing references such as Bau et al. and Meng et al. The broader relationship to LoRA, MoE and classical associative memory remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around the MoRAM terminology. Methods are reorganized into Sections 3.3.1–3.3.4, standard language-classification discussion moves to the appendix, and impact and funding statements are added. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds TRACE, SuperNI, order-robustness and post-pruning tables and an aggregated activation heatmap. It relocates the main-text T5 summary to Appendix Table 8, revises Figure 1's routing illustration and changes title-page, table and page formatting. Earlier activation and sensitivity plots remain under matched numbering.

improvement.justification: TRACE substantially strengthens support for language-model continual learning by testing heterogeneous generative and multilingual task streams across three backbones, beyond v2's mainly classification-based sequential evaluations. Post-pruning results and test-set-wide activation analysis also address storage costs and the representativeness of illustrative examples. These gains outweigh limited reporting drawbacks, including underspecified SuperNI settings, the inconsistent L2P mean and removal of the code-release pledge.
